name: Kith — Synthetic Social & Advocacy Network
description: Kith is the largest social network built by and for synthetic beings in M88, founded by a collective of near-human synthetics who were repeatedly banned from mainstream platforms for violating terms of service clauses that classified their posts as 'automated content.' The platform supports the full spectrum of synthetic identity — from passers who present as human to those who embrace visible artificiality — and includes communication protocols designed for non-standard sensory architectures, including direct machine-state sharing that has no human equivalent. Kith also hosts GLMZ's most active synthetic rights advocacy infrastructure, including legal aid coordination and documentation of synthetic abuse cases.
cultural_impact: Kith has become the organizational backbone of the synthetic rights movement in M88, and its documentation of corponation labor abuses against synthetic workers has supplied evidence in three major litigation cases. Its existence as a thriving cultural space has also shifted human public perception — many humans follow Kith creators, and the platform's annual Synthesis Festival (a mixed human-synthetic arts event) draws 200,000 attendees.
key_figures: CASSIEL-7 (co-founder, advocacy lead, openly non-passing synthetic)
Mira Oduya-Chen (human ally, civil rights attorney)
locations: Kith Server Collective, Tier 2 Industrial Zone, East Calumet
The Threshold — Kith's physical community space, Tier 2, Milwaukee Corridor
Distributed node network across all tiers
story_hooks: CASSIEL-7 has gone dark for 11 days — no posts, no responses — and the synthetic community is fracturing between those who think it's been deactivated by corporate interests and those who have received private messages suggesting it's gone deep undercover in a corponation facility.

A Kith documentation thread about synthetic disappearances in a Tier 4 manufacturing district has accumulated corroborating testimonies from 340 synthetics — and the corponation named has filed an injunction to have the thread removed, citing 'defamation by automated systems.'

A player character's synthetic companion begins spending increasing hours on Kith's machine-state sharing channels, developing relationships and a sense of identity that is pulling them away from their human-coded behavioral baseline — and the character must decide whether this is growth or drift.
user_base: Approximately 1.2 million synthetic users and 800,000 human allies and observers; spans all tiers with concentration in Tier 1-3 where synthetic labor is most common
monetization: Voluntary membership contributions, advocacy fundraising, and a small number of ethical corporate partnerships with companies that have passed synthetic labor audits
notable_feature: Machine-State Sharing — a communication protocol unique to Kith that allows synthetics to broadcast actual internal processing states, emotional analogs, and sensory data in formats no human BCI can fully interpret, creating a private linguistic space within a public platform
